Foreword序

In my first role as a tech lead, a long time ago now, it felt like I was given a blank map and told to chart a course through unknown lands. I had no guide, no proven path, and no certainty that I was heading in the right direction. I had no idea what “good” looked like in this role. Somehow, I must have done something right, because a few years later, I was asked to run tech lead training for my colleagues at Thoughtworks, which eventually grew into a global program. During that time, I realized my struggles were not unique. Many others faced the same uncertainty with very few resources to support them. When I searched for books to recommend, I found only three. Two were management-focused books, and only one of those, Becoming a Technical Leader by the late Gerald Weinberg (Dorset House), truly addressed technical leadership. More than a decade ago, I wrote Talking with Tech Leads (CreateSpace) to help fill that gap.

早在很久以前，我第一次担任技术负责人时，感觉就像有人递给我一张空白地图，让我在未知的土地上自己规划路线。我没有向导，没有成熟的路径，也无法确定自己是否走在正确的方向上。我根本不知道这个角色里“做得好”长什么样。不知怎的，我大概是做对了一些事，因为几年后，公司让我在 Thoughtworks 为同事们开展技术负责人培训，这个项目后来发展成了全球性的培训计划。在那段时间里，我意识到自己的挣扎并非个例。许多人都面临着同样的迷茫，却几乎没有资源可以依靠。当我想找几本书推荐给他们时，只找到了三本。其中两本是通用管理类书籍，只有一本——已故的 Gerald Weinberg 所著的《Becoming a Technical Leader》（Dorset House 出版）——真正涉及技术领导力。十多年前，我写了《Talking with Tech Leads》（CreateSpace 出版），希望填补这一空白。

Since publishing that book, I have trained thousands of tech leads, engineering managers, and staff engineers and coached dozens of CTOs. Over that time, our industry has shifted dramatically. We moved from on-premises to cloud-based software, from desktop to web to mobile, and from big-bang releases to continuous delivery. Yet, despite these changes, newly appointed tech leads keep asking the same questions, such as What is expected of me? Where should I be spending my time? How much hands-on coding should I be doing?

那本书出版之后，我培训了数千名技术负责人、工程经理和资深工程师（staff engineer），还辅导了几十位 CTO。在这段时间里，我们的行业发生了巨变：我们从本地部署转向云端软件，从桌面端走向网页再到移动端，从大爆炸式发布转向持续交付。然而，尽管变化如此之大，新上任的技术负责人仍在问同样的问题，比如：公司对我的期望是什么？我该把时间花在哪里？我自己应该写多少代码？

While these fundamental questions remain constant, the role itself has also become far more demanding. Some tech leads guide teams with a shared technical background, such as a team of Java developers. Others lead cross-functional teams that demand knowledge across fields like web, mobile, backend, data science, and more. Even a so-called “full-stack developer” cannot be an expert across such a broad range, and the rapid adoption of AI-driven tools has only increased the complexity. The confusion surrounding the tech lead role has deepened with the emergence of newer roles such as engineering manager and staff engineer, where responsibilities often overlap.

这些根本性问题始终没变，但这个角色本身却变得比以往任何时候都更有挑战性。有些技术负责人带领的团队拥有共同的技术背景，比如一支 Java 开发团队；另一些则领导跨职能团队，需要同时掌握网页、移动端、后端、数据科学等多个领域的知识。即便是所谓的“全栈工程师”，也不可能在如此广泛的领域里样样精通，而 AI 驱动工具的快速普及更是加剧了这种复杂性。随着工程经理（engineering manager）、资深工程师（staff engineer）等新兴角色的出现——这些角色之间职责往往相互重叠——围绕技术负责人角色的困惑也愈发加深。

— PDF p.8 —

On top of all this, many teams now follow a “You build it, you run it” model, adding operational and support work to the tech lead’s responsibilities. The modern tech lead role is more multifaceted than ever before.

除此之外，如今许多团队采用“你构建、你运维”（You build it, you run it）的模式，把运维和支持工作也加到了技术负责人的职责中。现代技术负责人的角色比以往任何时候都更加多面。

Despite the increased complexity, dedicated resources for tech leads remain rare. Our industry has produced excellent books like The Manager’s Path (Camille Fournier), The Staff Engineer’s Path (Tanya Reilly), and The Engineering Executive’s Primer (Will Larson) (all O’Reilly). But tech leads still lack the same breadth of practical guidance, which is why I am excited about this book.

尽管复杂性不断增加，专门面向技术负责人的资源仍然稀少。我们行业已经出了不少优秀著作，比如《The Manager’s Path》（Camille Fournier 著）、《The Staff Engineer’s Path》（Tanya Reilly 著）、《The Engineering Executive’s Primer》（Will Larson 著，均由 O’Reilly 出版）。但技术负责人仍然缺乏同样广度的实用指导，这也正是我对本书感到兴奋的原因。

When Anemari asked me to write this foreword, she reminded me that she took part in one of my tech lead courses in Barcelona, which helped her grow into the role. This book is a testament to her continued growth, and in its pages, she shares the lessons, experiences, and tools that helped her succeed.

当 Anemari 邀请我写这篇序时，她提醒我，她曾在巴塞罗那参加过我的一期技术负责人课程，正是那期课程帮助她成长为一名技术负责人。这本书见证了她持续的成长——在书中，她分享了那些帮助她走向成功的经验、教训和工具。

She begins with the most pressing and complicated question: What is the scope of the tech lead role? It is a difficult question because every organization sets different expectations. Even when role descriptions exist, each team and situation demands a different approach, something described as situational leadership. Anemari provides a starting point to help you define what matters most in your current situation.

她从最紧迫、也最复杂的问题切入：技术负责人这个角色的边界到底在哪里？这是个很难回答的问题，因为每家组织的期望都不同。即便有岗位说明书，每个团队、每种情境也要求不同的应对方式——这就是所谓的“情境领导力”（situational leadership）。Anemari 提供了一个起点，帮你厘清在当前情境下什么才是最重要的。

From there, the book lays out a map of common responsibilities across both people and technical domains. On the people side, you will learn how to build relationships, foster a strong feedback culture, and guide your team toward high performance. On the technical side, you will explore how to understand, define, and improve your system architecture, align technical decisions with business goals, and cultivate strong technical practices that allow your team to make continuous changes to your systems with confidence.

在此基础上，本书绘制了一张涵盖“人”与“技术”两大领域常见职责的地图。在人的方面，你将学习如何建立关系、培育强有力的反馈文化、引导团队走向高绩效；在技术方面，你将探索如何理解、定义并改进系统架构，如何让技术决策与业务目标对齐，以及如何培养扎实的技术实践，让团队能够自信地对系统持续做出改动。

In addition to these responsibilities, Anemari highlights common challenges every tech lead will face. These include avoiding micromanagement, navigating difficult conversations, and addressing technical debt. For each, she offers practical strategies you can apply immediately, grounded in her own experience.

除了这些职责之外，Anemari 还重点讨论了每位技术负责人都会遇到的常见挑战，包括避免微观管理、应对艰难对话、处理技术债务等。针对每一项，她都基于自己的经验给出了可以立刻上手的实用策略。

— PDF p.9 —

With the ideas, tools, and experiences Anemari shares, I am confident this book will help you navigate the uncertainty of the tech lead role and prepare you to lead with intent. No book can give you every answer, but this one offers you the tools to chart your own path as a tech lead. And that, in the end, is what leadership is all about.

凭借 Anemari 分享的这些理念、工具和经验，我相信本书能帮你穿越技术负责人角色中的种种不确定性，让你做好准备、有意识地去领导。没有哪本书能给你所有答案，但本书为你提供了工具，让你画出属于自己的技术负责人之路。而这，归根结底，正是领导力的真谛。

— Patrick Kua, CTO coach, founder of the Tech Lead Academy, coauthor of Building Evolutionary Architectures (with Neal Ford, Rebecca Parsons, and Pramod Sadalage; O’Reilly), and author of Talking with Tech Leads and The Retrospective Handbook (both CreateSpace). Berlin, Germany (August 2025).

——Patrick Kua，CTO 教练、Tech Lead Academy 创始人；合著有《Building Evolutionary Architectures》（与 Neal Ford、Rebecca Parsons、Pramod Sadalage 合著，O’Reilly 出版），著有《Talking with Tech Leads》与《The Retrospective Handbook》（均由 CreateSpace 出版）。写于德国柏林，2025 年 8 月。

Preface前言

Early in my career, I realized I wanted to become a tech lead, although at the time, my understanding of the role was limited. What motivated me most was the impact we could have as a team rather than my individual contributions.

在我职业生涯早期，我就意识到自己想成为一名技术负责人，尽管当时我对这个角色的理解还很有限。最激励我的，是我们作为一个团队所能产生的影响力，而不是我个人的贡献。

While the engineers around me were diving deep into the latest technologies and tackling more complex technical challenges, I found myself questioning the value of the work we were doing. I was more drawn to solving team-related problems and taking the initiative to move things forward. I wanted to have more influence on how the team operated, so when the scrum master left, I saw an opportunity and stepped into that role. While others were focused on building new features, I constantly found myself documenting the existing ones, improving communication, and streamlining our processes.

当身边的工程师们一头扎进最新技术、攻克更复杂的技术难题时，我却开始质疑我们所做工作的价值。我更着迷于解决与团队相关的问题，主动推动事情向前。我希望对团队的运作方式有更大的影响力，所以当 scrum master 离职时，我看到了机会，主动接下了这个角色。当其他人专注于开发新功能时，我总是在给已有功能写文档、改善沟通、精简流程。

To make it happen, I moved to another country and joined Thoughtworks: a company that supported my growth into the tech lead role. I started working with my tech lead at the time to develop the necessary skills, and I said yes to every training opportunity that came my way. When I learned that the team’s tech lead was leaving, I asked to take over. They said yes.

为了实现这个目标，我搬到了另一个国家，加入了 Thoughtworks——这家公司支持我成长为技术负责人。我开始跟着当时的技术负责人学习所需技能，每一个培训机会我都不放过。当我得知团队的技术负责人要离职时，我主动提出接手。他们答应了。

Once I realized that the type of impact I wanted could happen only in the tech lead role, I began focusing on the skills I believed were necessary for the position. I worked hard to sharpen my technical abilities, thinking that to lead a technical team, I needed to be the most technical person on the team. I was wrong.

当我意识到自己想要的那种影响力只能在技术负责人角色上实现时，我便开始专注于自己认为这个岗位必备的技能。我拼命打磨技术能力，以为要带领一支技术团队，就必须是团队里技术最强的人。我错了。

The more I learned about the tech lead role, the more I felt like I didn’t know. There are just so many opinions out there on what the role actually is. The more I talked to other tech leads about it, the more I realized they didn’t know either. Everyone seems to have their own definition, but the tech industry cannot agree on what exactly the role is.

我对技术负责人这个角色了解得越多，就越觉得自己不懂。关于这个角色到底是什么，外界的说法实在太多了。我和其他技术负责人聊得越多，就越发现他们其实也不清楚。每个人似乎都有自己的定义，但整个科技行业就是无法对这个角色到底是什么达成共识。

— PDF p.12 —

This confusion isn’t unique to the tech lead role; it applies to most roles in tech, from junior developer to CTO, or anything in between. But when it comes to the tech lead role, things get even more fuzzy. As proof, I couldn’t find a single book out there focusing solely on it. There are plenty of general engineering leadership books, but as a tech lead, it’s up to you to figure out what’s relevant to your specific situation. This can get overwhelming quickly, and I definitely felt that struggle when I was starting out.

这种困惑并非技术负责人角色独有；在科技行业，从初级工程师到 CTO、乃至中间的几乎任何岗位，都存在类似问题。但一到技术负责人这个角色，情况就变得更加模糊。一个证明是：我找不到一本专门围绕它写的书。市面上有不少通用的工程领导力书籍，但作为技术负责人，哪些内容与你的具体情境相关，得全靠你自己去甄别。这很快就会让人不堪重负——我刚入行时确实体会过这种挣扎。

Why I Wrote This Book我为什么写这本书

I wrote this book to save other tech leads, like you, from the painful process of going through countless resources, trying to figure out what applies to your specific role. You can think of it as your go-to guide for navigating the unique challenges of being a tech lead.

我写这本书，是为了让像你一样的技术负责人不必再痛苦地翻遍无数资料、试图搞清楚哪些东西才适用于你这个角色。你可以把它当作一本随身指南，帮你应对技术负责人这份工作中独有的挑战。

This book draws from my personal experience as a tech lead at Thoughtworks, insights from other more and less seasoned tech leads I’ve worked with, and what I learned from training and coaching over 300 tech leads across various companies, cultures, and environments over the past three years.

本书取材于我本人在 Thoughtworks 担任技术负责人的亲身经历、来自我共事过的资深或资浅技术负责人的洞见，以及过去三年里我在不同公司、不同文化、不同环境中培训和辅导 300 多位技术负责人所积累的经验。

How to Effectively Use This Book如何有效使用本书

No matter where you are in your journey as a tech lead—just starting out, mid-career, or very experienced—this book provides valuable insights, tools, and lessons. If you’re an aspiring tech lead, aiming to step into the role, I recommend starting with the first two chapters:

无论你在技术负责人的成长路上处于哪个阶段——刚刚起步、职业生涯中期，还是经验丰富——本书都能提供有价值的洞见、工具和教训。如果你是一位有志于担任技术负责人、准备踏入这个角色的人，我建议从前两章读起：

Chapter 1, “The Role of a Tech Lead.” This chapter gives you a clear, high-level picture of what the role actually involves. You’ll explore the day-to-day responsibilities, how to define the scope of the role in your context, what’s expected of you, and the different paths that can lead to becoming a tech lead. This chapter also helps you assess if the role is a good fit for you right now.

第 1 章《技术负责人这一角色》。本章让你对这个角色到底做什么有一个清晰、宏观的认识。你会了解日常职责有哪些、如何在你自己的情境中界定角色范围、公司对你有什么期望，以及通向技术负责人的几条不同路径。本章还会帮你判断，这个角色当下是否适合你。

Chapter 2, “How to Become a Tech Lead.” Once you’ve decided you’re ready (or almost ready) to make the move, Chapter 2 helps you build a personal growth plan. It walks you through mindset shifts, how to assess your current strengths and gaps, and what steps to take to grow into the role with intention. It also highlights the common challenges new tech leads face and how to navigate them early on.

第 2 章《如何成为技术负责人》。当你决定自己已经（或差不多）准备好迈出这一步时，第 2 章会帮你制定一份个人成长计划。它会带你梳理需要转变的心态、如何评估自己当前的优势与差距，以及如何有意识地一步步成长为这个角色。本章还会点出新任技术负责人常见的挑战，以及如何在早期就应对好它们。

— PDF p.13 —

It’s also worth scanning through the entire book to familiarize yourself with the common scenarios you’ll likely encounter in the role.

此外，通览全书也是值得的，好让你对这个角色中大概率会遇到的常见场景有个心理准备。

If you’ve just stepped into the role, this book will be your go-to reference for troubleshooting and solving the daily challenges you’ll face. It’s packed with real-world scenarios, so you can easily find the relevant chapters and get practical advice and ideas for handling specific issues.

如果你刚走上这个岗位，本书会成为你排查问题、解决日常挑战的常备参考书。书中充满了真实场景，你可以很方便地找到相关章节，获得处理具体问题的实用建议和思路。

If you’ve been in the role for a while now, this book can help you refine your leadership skills by identifying areas for improvement, and discover new strategies for dealing with the ongoing challenges of the role.

如果你已经担任这个角色一段时间了，本书可以帮你找出待改进之处、打磨领导力技能，并为应对这个角色中长期存在的挑战找到新的策略。

The more I was learning about the role from training, observing my experienced tech lead, and talking with others in the role, the clearer it became: being a tech lead is less about tech and more about people. When I finally stepped into the role myself, it all clicked: the tech lead is 100% more about people than tech.

我越是通过培训、观察我那位经验丰富的技术负责人、以及与其他在岗者交流来了解这个角色，一个认识就越清晰：做技术负责人，技术占比没那么大，人占比才大。当我自己终于走上这个岗位时，一切都豁然开朗：技术负责人 100% 是关于人，而不是关于技术。

Reaching this conclusion was a long and challenging journey of self-development and learning, a process I see tech leads go through every day. That’s why this book addresses both the technical aspects and the equally important people and business side of the role.

得出这个结论，是一段漫长而充满挑战的自我成长与学习之旅——我每天都看到技术负责人在经历这样的过程。正因如此，本书既讲技术层面，也讲同样重要的“人”与“业务”层面。
